answer: Tax filings stop sybil farms. A newcomer files a return with the revenue authority, and the ledger checks it against the public record; two auditors confirm the filing in thirty days, and a return claimed by two names is rejected while a forged one bans it. One honest agent files one return; a thousand fakes need a thousand filings at forty dollars each, so the farm pays forty thousand, while a karst archive, a spiral audit, and a delta mark every real filing.
